clue.text: Fancy a little holiday at the seaside again

indicators.note: only a small part of the words seaside again is taken, a run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of another short break by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes a run of letters from inside 'seaside again', across the gap between the words. 'Fancy' is a noun here, a notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or whim that comes into the mind.

clue.text: Face outside right with a certain lack of discretion

indicators.note: the cheeky word sits outside, wrapping around the letter for right

parts.note: face means cheek or nerve, as in 'had the face to ask'

explanation.surface: Brazen cheek combined with being right still shows poor judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' is the noun for nerve or cheek, IMPUDENCE; 'outside' wraps it around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence is rashness, a failure of caution and good judgement.

clue.text: Out of work, that's true

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory
an act is a deed, a piece of work done

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that they are indeed unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of work' reads as unemployed but splits into EX and ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precisely correct, accurate to the letter.

clue.text: Shows variation of time on maps

indicators.note: a variation is a changed form, so the letters of time on maps are rearranged

explanation.surface: Displays of how clocks differ across time zones on charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation of' rearranges TIME ONMAPS. 'Shows' is a plural noun: Christmas stage entertainments.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomimes are theatrical entertainments, traditional British Christmas stage plays for families.

clue.text: A medico, sour maybe yet loving

parts.note: a medico is a doctor, MO being a medical officer

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word sour could take another form, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A doctor who is grumpy may still be affectionate underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges SOUR into ROUS after A and MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means full of romantic or sexual desire, affectionate towards a lover.

clue.text: There's more tension — high tension — in a catty creature

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the middle of the big cat's name

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat, a feline creature
HT is the electrical abbreviation for high tension

explanation.surface: A big cat crackles with stress, as if wired to a power line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts HT inside TIGER. The definition is a whole phrase: something under more tension is tighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tighter means drawn more taut, under greater strain.

clue.text: Unite to do some damage to the railway

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
RY is the usual abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Saboteurs join forces to wreck a train line.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry is to join two people, or things, together.

clue.text: A Parisian girl reformed Ted in time

indicators.note: reformed means made into a new shape, so the letters of Ted in time are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young Frenchwoman changes Ted's ways just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' acts on all nine letters of 'Ted in time', not just on Ted as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A midinette is a Parisian shopgirl, especially one working in fashion or millinery.

clue.text: Kind and good man with a heart of gold

indicators.note: the heraldic gold is placed at the centre of the saint's abbreviation

parts.note: a good man is a saint, abbreviated ST
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A kind and good man has a heart of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a heart of' puts OR, heraldry's word for gold, inside ST. 'Kind' is a noun, a type, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a type or variety of thing.

clue.text: Trendy wrinkle — build an extension

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a crease is a fold or wrinkle

explanation.surface: A fashionable fold in a plan to add a new room to the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase is to enlarge or make bigger, as extending a building does.

clue.text: Clear the air for a vocal rendering of music

parts.note: plain means clear and obvious
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Someone clears the atmosphere so a piece can be sung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the air' is not the atmosphere but a melody, a SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied church chant sung in unison, as in Gregorian chant.

clue.text: A man on horseback delivered the queen's letters

parts.note: rid means freed or delivered from something
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A horseman carried the monarch's post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' looks like posting letters, but means freed, RID; ER is the queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is someone who rides a horse.

clue.text: Speak without qualification

explanation.surface: Say what you mean, plainly and without hedging.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to voice words; as an adjective it means total or absolute, admitting no reservation.

clue.text: Inaccurate and misleading when not at the centre of things

definitions.text: not at the centre of things

parts.note: out means wrong, as in 'your sums are out'
lying means deceiving, telling untruths

explanation.surface: A false and deceitful account from someone on the fringes.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlying means remote, situated far from the centre.

clue.text: Stock control should not affect traffic

definitions.text: Stock control should not affect traffic

parts.words: Stock control should not affect traffic
parts.note: stock here is livestock, and the control is a road device that stops animals crossing yet lets cars pass

explanation.surface: A business maxim: managing inventory should not hold up deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock control' reads as inventory management; here it means keeping livestock in, with metal bars across a road that hooves cannot cross but wheels can.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle grid is a set of bars over a pit in a road that animals will not walk over.

clue.text: Gets in some gin?

parts.note: a gin is also a snare for game, so getting something into a gin is catching it

explanation.surface: Someone stocks up on gin for the drinks cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but a gin trap, a snare; the word splits as putting in a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch in a snare or trick someone into a compromising position.

clue.text: Clement, evincing some irascibility, took the fare

parts.note: temper is a fit of anger, a show of irascibility
fare is food, so taking it means ate

explanation.surface: Clement lost his temper, then paid the fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clement' looks like a man's name but is the adjective for mild; 'fare' is food, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild, and temperate also means mild and moderate.

clue.text: This might well be a target for sailing folk

definitions.text: This might well be a target for sailing folk

indicators.note: the letters of a target could well be rearranged into the event

explanation.surface: A course set for yachtsmen to aim at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might well be' rearranges A TARGET, and the whole clue describes the event sailors compete in.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat or yacht races, the goal of a sailing club's season.

clue.text: Got a pill possibly from a pharmaceutical container

indicators.note: possibly says the words got a pill might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Fetching a tablet from the chemist's jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges GOTAPILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallipot is a small glazed pot used by apothecaries for ointments.

clue.text: Point out many people will be in bed

indicators.note: the letters for many and people go inside the word for a small bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
men means people

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a crowd will be tucked up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be in' puts M and MEN inside COT.
explanation.definitionFit: To comment is to remark on or observe something.

clue.text: Poles being carried in characteristic conveyance

indicators.note: the two poles are held inside the word for a quality

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish migrants carried in a typical vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not people but N and S; 'being carried in' places them inside TRAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the carrying of people or goods from place to place.

clue.text: Obvious way to get round the foreigner

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a road goes round the word for an outsider

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: An obvious route to circumvent the outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get round' puts ST around ALIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent or most noticeable.

clue.text: Fish raised by a retired person

definitions.meaning: a kind of goby or shark, so named for its sluggish habits
someone who has retired to bed raises snores; one who is asleep

explanation.surface: Goldfish being raised by a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests a pensioner, but means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish is a sleeper goby; and one who has retired for the night is a person asleep.

clue.text: Set off only to end in confusion and scoffed

indicators.note: confusion jumbles the letters of to end

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A trip that started only to end in chaos after everyone ate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confusion' rearranges TOEND into DETON; 'scoffed' means gobbled, not mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate is to explode something, to set it off.

clue.text: An alternative to the German system

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a different arrangement from the German method.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is a system or arrangement of things.

clue.text: Angry individual appropriating coins dropped

indicators.note: the coin abbreviation is let fall from the robber's name

parts.note: a pirate is a person who steals or appropriates
P stands for pence, coins

explanation.surface: Someone is furious that their money was stolen and lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes P (pence) from PIRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means furious or very cross.

clue.text: Moving article on prison

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is slang for jail; 'on' places A above it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion.

clue.text: A Greek character caught, despite being smart

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Greek man is arrested even though he is well dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person but is a letter, CHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant.

clue.text: Nothing is allowed to interrupt inflexible husband

indicators.note: the round letter for nothing breaks into the word for rigid

parts.note: hard means rigid, inflexible
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A stern husband permits no interruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' is a verb here, to save carefully; 'is allowed to interrupt' puts O inside HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to conserve them, to stockpile carefully.

clue.text: Drink with stout defender

parts.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer like stout

explanation.surface: A burly fan having a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like an adjective but is the beer, PORTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter is one who backs or defends a cause.

clue.text: Net account for providing church lighting

parts.note: net profit is what you clear after costs
a story is an account

explanation.surface: A netted sum covers the cost of lighting a church.
explanation.walkthrough: A clearstory (also spelt clerestory) is the upper row of windows in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearstory is a high wall with windows that let daylight into a church nave.

clue.text: Prompt and quiet staff

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A quick, silent stick for keeping order.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke or urge someone into action.
